reason_summary: No extracted estimate is pre-modern: the only PM-touching row is Basso, Bodenhorn and Cuberes (US counties, 1850, classified PM|FDT), a cross-sectional bank-presence regression rated serious risk of bias whose own rationale concedes county bank placement is plausibly endogenous to fertility-relevant development. That is correlational evidence for a speculative mechanism, which is PROTOCOL 4.1 'very low'. No decomposition share, slope sufficiency or R-squared exists for PM, so none of the three 4.2 criteria has been evaluated and the significance question is unanswered rather than answered negatively.

I verified the favourable risk-of-bias pattern: the three moderate-rated Cell A studies (Danzer-Zyska, Rossi-Godard, Billari-Galasso) all point the hypothesised way once oriented, while the six serious-rated ones split three ways (Shen, Fenge-Scheubel and Basso negative; Han and Galofre-Vila positive; Guinnane-Streb null at p=0.22). But the two moderate studies that are FDT-classified are contemporary developing-country pension expansions (Namibia, Brazil), not the Western FDT, and every study inside the historical FDT window is serious-rated and inconsistent, so 'replicated and broadly consistent' fails and the rating stops below moderate. Escalating because I reproduced both pooled summaries exactly and the completed-fertility pool is 88.3% Billari-Galasso (an SDT-classified Italian study) and flips from -0.0677 to +0.0549 if Galofre-Vila's same-unit, more precise estimate is admitted; that pool cannot bear the FDT sentence it is cited for, and the orientation exclusion is a PI call. No slope sufficiency was computed for FDT and the demographic-significance file lists computing it as the next required step, so 'partial' is not supported.

The below-replacement Cell A evidence is one moderate-rated rich-country quasi-experiment (Billari-Galasso, Italy) plus two serious-rated Chinese studies that contradict each other: Shen's NRPS estimate is negative (-0.169 children) while Han's long-term-care estimate is positive (+4.0pp), and I confirmed Han enters the birth-probability pool against the hypothesised direction. One credible quasi-experiment without consistent replication is PROTOCOL 4.1 'low'. I rate not significant rather than insufficient data because the slope argument runs one way qualitatively: mature systems leave almost no new variation on this margin, and the mechanism predicts that the SDT era's pension retrenchment should have raised fertility, whereas fertility fell. Escalating because demographic-significance.csv flags this row needs_human_review=yes and PROTOCOL 2 reserves policy-constrained low-fertility settings for human review, and dropping China leaves the cell with a single study.

I verified that none of Eibich-Siedler, Ilciukas or Akyol-Atalay appears among the ten rows of fulltext-screen.csv, and that all eight of their effect rows are the only extractions in the chapter carrying ra_verified=no. The three designs are individually good and agree in direction, which would support moderate, but a channel whose entire evidence base was hand-picked outside the documented search has no PRISMA denominator and an unquantifiable selection risk, so I rate down one step. I also verified the magnitude support is not a decomposition: the sufficiency file divides a per-year-of-delay IV coefficient, and in two rows a birth probability, by a Netherlands TFR decline of just 0.0973 over 2004-2021, producing shares up to 273.4%, and both companion notes state the actual scaling is still future work. A share above 100% is evidence the quantity is not a share. Eibich-Siedler's outcome is also a birth in year t+1, which cannot distinguish tempo from quantum.
